content.text: A **proof** derives a conclusion from premises one step at a time. Each step names a rule and the lines it uses.

content.definition: From P → Q and P, infer Q.
From P ∧ Q, infer P, or infer Q.

examples.title: A short proof
examples.note: Every line follows from lines above it.

examples.title: Working backward
lines: R would follow from Q → R if we had Q.
Q would follow from P → Q and P.
examples.note: Ask what would give you the goal, then what would give you that.

question.prompt: What does modus ponens let you infer?
options: Q from P → Q and P
question.hint: Modus ponens uses a conditional together with its if part.
question.explanation: From P → Q and P, modus ponens infers Q.
